entries.label: 2026 federal income tax brackets, by upper threshold (upper null = no limit)
entries.notes: First full year at 14% bottom rate (2025 was a blended 14.5% after the mid-year cut from 15% effective Jul 1, 2025). All thresholds indexed up 2.0% for 2026. 2027 brackets land ~Dec 2026; rollover watch owns refresh.
entries.source_note: CRA official rates index. 2026 brackets cross-checked unanimously across 5 independent sources 2026-09-27 (FiscalFold, money.ca, immigrationnewscanada.ca, getgis.org, UBM Tax) plus KPMG June-30-2026 federal/provincial tables and Fidelity 2026 brackets page.

entries.label: 2026 federal indexation factor
entries.source_note: CRA 2026 indexation factor, corroborated by federal-tax-brackets-2026-research.md.

entries.label: 2026 federal basic personal amount (maximum)
entries.notes: Enhanced BPA phases down for net income above $181,440, settling at a base of ~$14,829 for income above $258,482 (full BPA for net income <= $181,440). Earn $16,452 or less and federal tax is $0.
entries.source_note: Verified 2026-09-27 across multiple 2026 tax guides (Fidelity, Waypoint Budget, Lifemoney, money.ca). Credit value = BPA x 14% = $2,303.28.

entries.label: 2026 federal basic personal amount (reduced base for high earners)
entries.source_note: UBM Tax + money.ca, verified 2026-09-27: full BPA at net income <= $181,440; reduced $14,829 above $258,482.

entries.label: 2026 federal charitable donation credit rates
entries.notes: 33% applies on donations above $200 when taxable income exceeds $258,482.

entries.label: 2025 federal brackets (history row for year-over-year copy)
entries.notes: Bottom-rate cut 15% -> 14.5% blended took effect Jul 1, 2025 (Bill C-4). Saving from the 14% full-year rate vs old 15% at >= $58,523 income: ~$585/yr federally on that first slice.
entries.source_note: From federal-tax-brackets-2026-research.md (2026-09-27): 2025 BPA max was $16,129; 2025 indexation 1.9%; bottom rate blended 14.5%.
